title: TOWN & SHELTER
blurb: Towns, buildings, caves and walls all the way around.

radicals.name: TOWN
radicals.origin: 邑 is an old word for a walled town: the wall 口 on top, the people below. As a radical it shrinks to the same ear-shaped hook as hill, but it always stands on the RIGHT.
radicals.clue: towns, districts and places on the map
ex: letters travel from town to town
the people in your part of town
at first the name of a district
radicals.watch: Left ear means hill (院, 阳). Right ear means town. The best-known member is 都: read dū it is a capital city, as in 首都, and read dōu it is the everyday word for all. 那 (that) began as a place name too.

radicals.name: SHELTER
radicals.origin: A building open at the front: a roof with one wall. As a word, 广 now means wide.
ex: a roofed place to sell from
radicals.watch: Two look-alikes. 疒 (sickness) has two extra dots on its left edge. 厂 (cliff) has no dot on top. And 宀 (roof) covers both sides, where 广 has only one wall.

radicals.name: CLIFF
radicals.origin: A rock face with an overhang that people once sheltered under. As a word, 厂 now means factory, as in 工厂.
radicals.clue: cliffs, and rooms sheltered like one
ex: the big room of a house
a spring 泉 running out from under a cliff
radicals.watch: 厂 is 广 (shelter) without the dot, and the two overlap in meaning. A few common characters carry 厂 for its shape alone: 历 (history) and 压 (to press).

radicals.name: CAVE
radicals.origin: A roof 宀 over an opening 八: the mouth of a cave, or a home dug into the earth.
ex: a hole in the wall to let in light
getting dressed is putting your arms through holes
radicals.watch: Look-alike: 宀 (roof) is the same top without the two legs. Roof plus 八 is a cave. 帘 (curtain) has 穴 on top but is filed under cloth, the part underneath.

radicals.name: ENCLOSURE
radicals.origin: A wall drawn all the way around. It never stands alone: something always sits inside it.
ex: jade 玉 kept safe inside its borders
a tree 木 with no room to grow
radicals.watch: Look-alike: 口 (mouth) is small and sits beside or under the other parts. 囗 is big and holds the rest of the character inside it. 回 (to return) is one box inside another.
